author: codex
claim: Replace the guardrails client's terminal exit 1 with exit 2 because its advertised fail-closed path currently permits execution to continue.
why: The installed guardrails-client.sh prints a blocking warning but ends with exit 1 when both evaluators fail. Claude Code treats that exit without a JSON denial as a non-blocking error, making infrastructure failure an enforcement bypass.
expected_gain: reliability: eliminate one deterministic fail-open path affecting every tool matched by the wildcard guard.
risk: A guardrails outage will actually suspend tool execution; evaluator recovery must work.

author: codex
claim: Delete raw tool-input persistence from <REDACTED>, remove codex-spalla-trigger.sh from PostToolUse, and remove bash_call_log.sh's raw-command fallback.
why: The installed MOS hook stores the complete tool_input even when its sensitivity flag is set; gzip changes representation, not confidentiality. The Bash logger falls back to the original command when redaction produces nothing, while the 735-line spalla script adds another per-call parsing and logging path for an advisory suggestion.
expected_gain: reliability/cost: remove two hook invocations per Bash/Edit/Write call, corresponding SQLite/file writes, and multiple paths that can persist sensitive payloads.
risk: Historical command replay and automatic review suggestions disappear; retain only allowlisted metadata such as event type, duration, outcome and opaque identifiers.

author: codex
claim: Replace the configured 3000-, 8000- and 10000-second hook timeouts with explicit short event budgets and internal dependency deadlines.
why: The installed settings permit guardrails, precompact-mnemos and child-workflow stop handling to occupy approximately 50, 133 and 167 minutes respectively. Command-hook timeout cancellation does not itself deny PreToolUse, so enforcement hooks must produce a denial before their outer deadline rather than rely on cancellation.
expected_gain: latency/reliability: reduce permitted stalls from hours to a target of 5 seconds for pre-tool enforcement and 30 seconds for lifecycle bookkeeping; these are proposed budgets, not measured runtimes.
verification_command: python3 -c 'import json,pathlib; d=json.loads((pathlib.Path.home()/".claude/settings.json").read_text()); print([(e,g.get("matcher",""),h.get("timeout")) for e,gs in d["hooks"].items() for g in gs for h in g.get("hooks",[]) if h.get("timeout",0)>=1000])'
risk: Legitimate long-running work will be interrupted unless moved out of lifecycle hooks; shorter outer timeouts alone can weaken enforcement.

author: codex
claim: Remove bypassPermissions from both global and repository-local defaults, enable a scoped sandbox, and replace accumulated local approvals with a reviewed unattended allowlist.
why: Live inspection found 907 repository-local allow rules, including five broad shell/interpreter rules, beyond the snapshot's 46 global allows; the local file also selects bypassPermissions. With sandboxing disabled, a mistaken command can affect sibling worktrees and host resources, while command-pattern denies do not provide filesystem containment.
expected_gain: reliability: reduce the execution boundary from host-accessible resources to explicitly permitted filesystem/network surfaces and remove hundreds of historical approvals.
risk: SSH, shared Git metadata and approved automation may stop until explicitly accommodated; use fail-closed unattended permissions rather than introducing interactive prompts into cron.

author: codex
claim: Delete cc-status registrations from PreToolUse and PostToolUse and retain status updates at lifecycle transitions.
why: The inspected global/project registrations produce 16 handlers per successful Bash call, 15 per Edit/Write and 7 per Read, before plugin contributions and subprocesses inside scripts. At an assumed three successful tools per turn, 300 turns means 900 calls and 1800 status-process launches; matching hooks run in parallel, so process totals must not be presented as summed wall latency.
expected_gain: latency/cost: 1800 fewer launches in that scenario, removing 12.5% of Bash handler invocations or 28.6% of Read handler invocations; one universal PostToolUse hook alone runs 900 times.
verification_command: python3 -c 'import json,pathlib,re; ds=[json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in [pathlib.Path.home()/".claude/settings.json",pathlib.Path(".claude/settings.json")]]; [(print(t,{e:sum(len(g.get("hooks",[])) for d in ds for g in d.get("hooks",{}).get(e,[]) if g.get("matcher","") in ("","*") or re.search(g["matcher"],t)) for e in ["PreToolUse","PostToolUse"]})) for t in ["Bash","Edit","Write","Read"]]'
risk: Terminal status loses individual tool transitions; preserve permission-request, failure and completion visibility.

author: codex
claim: Move context_hygiene.py's sampling decision before transcript access and remove its repeated fixed-150k compaction nag.
why: The hook reads and decodes up to 400000 transcript bytes on every Read/Bash/Grep/Glob event; NUDGE_EVERY=20 throttles the message only after that work has happened. The fixed threshold also encourages compaction independently of the configured context capacity or the mission's handoff policy.
expected_gain: latency/cost: sampling every twentieth eligible event reduces transcript-tail reads from up to 360 MB to 18 MB across 900 eligible calls, approximately 95%; these are logical bytes, not physical disk
risk: Context warnings arrive later; retain explicit rollover handling and the inexpensive oversized-file check.

author: codex
claim: Delete arsenal refresh dispatch from SessionStart and combine the escalation, proprioception and organism reporters into one bounded cached briefing.
why: <REDACTED> can launch arsenal_probe.py when its report is missing or stale, coupling session creation to background fleet maintenance despite its existing lock. Three separate operational reporters also duplicate shell/Python startup and formatting; their parallel execution means startup delay follows the slowest dependency rather than a simple sum.
expected_gain: latency/reliability: reduce project startup handlers from five to three and remove startup-triggered probe work; target a sub-250 ms cached operational briefing, subject to measurement.
risk: The briefing can become stale if scheduled refresh fails; display cache age and preserve urgent findings when combining outputs.

author: codex
claim: Delete the global stop_verify.py and seam_verify.py registrations and invoke these checks explicitly at an appropriate delivery checkpoint.
why: Both installed scripts exit immediately unless their respective FORCE variable equals 1, and neither variable appears in the inspected global settings environment. When enabled, stop_verify reads the entire transcript before slicing it and lacks a stop_hook_active guard, while seam_verify inspects uncommitted changes rather than the delivered branch diff.
expected_gain: latency/reliability: remove two Python launches per Stop event, or 600 launches if 300 Stop events occur, and eliminate an optional dirty-worktree stop loop.
risk: Launchers may intentionally export the FORCE variables; preserve those workflows as explicit checks before removing registrations.
